Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

wrong adjective and adverb

incorrect, mistaken

also be wrong, wrongly, by mistake, you’re wrong, get it wrong, mistaken, incorrect, you’re making a big mistake, you’re very wrong, false, falsely

classical

Ter. Heaut. 105: Errās, sī id crēdis
Cic. Tusc. 1.39: errāre mehercule mālō cum Platōne
Traupman 409: be wrong, errāre
Cic. Arch. 22: vehementer errat (Lewis & Short s.v. nam)
Traupman 104: you’re making a big mistake, errās pervērsē; vehementer errās

errō, errāre, errāvī, errātum

verb, first conjugation, intransitive

be wrong, be mistaken

“You’re wrong” is errās; badly wrong, longē errāre (Ter. Ad. 65) or tōtā errāre viā (Ter. Eun. 245).

Other words

  • perperam — wrongly, wrong; by mistake

    adverb · classical · Plaut. Most. 968: nē ad aliās aedīs perperam dēvēnerīs; Cic. Quinct. 31: seu rēctē seu perperam facere coepērunt; Traupman 409: if I have done anything wrong, I’m sorry, sī quid perperam fēcī, mē paenitet; Traupman 104: by mistake, imprūdēns, perperam

    The opposite of rēctē. Where English says “the wrong house”, Latin puts the mistake in the verb, as Plautus does.

  • falsus, falsa, falsum — wrong, untrue (of what is said or believed)

    also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 2.28: falsum est enim … id tōtum; Traupman 409: wrong (incorrect, mistaken), falsus; Traupman 155, 152; Traupman 195: falsely, falsō

    Of a statement or a belief: falsum est, that isn’t true. Of a person, “mistaken” (Sall. J. 85.20, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Ita dīcō, nē ad aliās aedīs perperam dēvēnerīs.

    I’m telling you so that you don’t go to the wrong house by mistake.Plaut. Most. 968

  • Errās, sī id crēdis, et mē ignōrās, Clīnia.

    You’re wrong if you believe that, and you don’t know me, Clinia.Ter. Heaut. 105

  • errāre mehercule mālō cum Platōne … quam cum istīs vēra sentīre

    I’d rather be wrong with Plato, by Hercules, … than be right with that crowdCic. Tusc. 1.39

  • Errābās, Verrēs, et vehementer errābās.

    You were wrong, Verres, very wrong.Cic. Verr. 2.5.121 (Lewis & Short s.v. et)

See also wrong, true, that’s right, what’s the matter?.
